A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpaceDrive. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes planning, Bench2Drive simulation, counterfactual reasoning and ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds depth-pooling comparisons, depth-error experiments and normalization-parameter convergence observations.

M1.justification: The spatial encoding, minimum-depth pooling, token injection, coordinate decoder and training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 newly explains coordinate parsing; the PDFs do not establish a changed parsing procedure. Alternative pooling strategies are ablations, not replacements of the proposed method.

E1.justification: nuScenes, OmniDrive VQA data and Bench2Drive remain the datasets and tasks. Appendix B.3 additionally evaluates biased and randomly perturbed depth estimates, extending test coverage to controlled depth-error conditions without adding a dataset or driving domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 newly includes Drive-WM in its stated OmniDrive/ORION-protocol comparison; v1 included it only in the appendix's ST-P3-metric comparison. X-Driver and GEMINUS disappear from main Table 2 but remain in the comprehensive appendix comparison, so their results are not removed from the paper.

E3.justification: New experiments compare minimum, average and median depth pooling and distinguish perturbations during training plus inference from inference-only perturbations. Table H specifies 5% perturbations for the former and 2.5% for the latter, although B.3 describes 5% for both. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, backbones and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a pooling-strategy ablation (Table D), a depth-error robustness study (Table H), and normalization convergence observations (A.3). These are focused additions to the retained component ablations, backbone comparisons, trajectory analyses and qualitative driving cases.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 888 and report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new normalization-factor range describes variation across backbones and settings, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes ST-P3's average L2 from 2.65 to 2.11 m and collision rate from 4.23% to 0.71%, without explaining the replacement. New pooling results show L2 of 1.80 for minimum versus 1.83 for average and median pooling; inference-only perturbations retain L2 of 1.80. A.3 newly reports convergence to 0.087 in the default setting. SpaceDrive's headline benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3's encoding, injection, decoding and loss equations (1)-(8) and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the unified spatial-representation contribution, claimed state-of-the-art nuScenes performance and second-best VLM-based Bench2Drive performance. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges minimum pooling's outlier sensitivity and explains tradeoffs against averaging and median pooling. B.3 newly interprets robustness as reliance on spatial structure, with semantic understanding compensating for depth errors. Existing limitations concerning uncertainty handling and temporal memory remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement with a direct repository link. Appendix A.1 specifies coordinate-format matching, zero-padding of two-dimensional coordinates and ordinary tokenization of unmatched numbers. A.3 supplies learned normalization values. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: The same 84 references and related-work discussion remain. Positioning changes locally: GEMINUS moves from the VLM-based category in v1 Table H to the traditional-modular category in v2 Table J, and Section 4.2 calls OmniDrive the codebase rather than the base model.

P1.justification: v2 expands the appendix with parsing explanations and new convergence and robustness subsections, alongside limited main-text wording and correspondence-detail edits. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Two appendix tables are added for pooling and depth errors. Existing tables are renumbered and relocated, and the main benchmark tables receive row and sizing changes. The original figures and qualitative panels are retained; the overall visual design remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicit parsing rules, convergence information, code-access information and focused pooling/depth-error experiments modestly improve reproducibility and support for the existing design. These gains are limited by reporting ambiguities: B.3 describes 5% perturbations while Table H lists 2.5% for inference-only tests, and revised Table 1 ST-P3 values match the appendix's differently labeled protocol without explanation. The core method and headline performance evidence remain unchanged.
